subject: Archaeology
title: The Brothels and Bathhouses of Pompeii
description: A quick win: understand The Brothels and Bathhouses of Pompeii.

hook.text: Pompeii had at least 25 brothels for a city of 11,000 people. Romans had a very different view of vice.

buildup.text: The main brothel, the Lupanare, had stone beds and explicit frescoes serving as a menu for clients.

discovery.text: Public bathhouses served as social clubs. Rich and poor bathed together in heated pools with mosaic floors.

twist.text: Bath water was rarely changed. Archaeologists found evidence of parasites — Roman hygiene was less clean than it looked.

climax.text: These buildings reveal a society where public and private life blurred in ways modern visitors find surprising.

punchline.text: Romans bathed together, socialized naked, and called it civilization.

quiz.question: What did archaeological analysis of Roman bathhouses reveal?
options: They were strictly segregated by social class
Bath water was rarely changed and contained parasites
Only wealthy citizens were allowed to use the heated pools

details.summary: Pompeii's lupanare (brothel) and numerous bathhouses reveal the social life of a Roman city in intimate detail. Erotic frescoes, changing rooms with cubby holes, heated pools, and exercise yards show how Romans blended hygiene, socializing, and entertainment into daily routines.
details.whyItMatters: Bath culture was central to Roman identity, cutting across class lines. Studying these buildings reveals how Romans experienced leisure, socialized across social boundaries, and constructed public and private spaces.
takeaways: Pompeii's brothel and baths are preserved in remarkable detail
Bathhouses combined hygiene, exercise, and social gathering
These buildings reveal Roman social life across class boundaries

faq.question: How did Roman bathhouses work?
faq.answer: Bathers moved through rooms of increasing temperature — the frigidarium (cold), tepidarium (warm), and caldarium (hot) — heated by underfloor hypocaust systems. Baths included exercise areas, gardens, libraries, and food vendors, functioning as social clubs open to all classes.

faq.question: What do the Pompeii erotic frescoes reveal?
faq.answer: The brothel's frescoes likely served as a visual menu of services. Beyond the lupanare, erotic imagery appears throughout Pompeii in homes and businesses. This prevalence shows that Roman attitudes toward sexuality were far more open than later European cultures.
